import sys, json, re

# Two phases on one cell -- and a THIRD branch that exists because the naive
# two-phase shape loops. If phase B is "anything that is not a fresh request",
# then a store error reply is read as a fresh
# request, re-queried from the error text, and the pair spins until the TTL
# kills it. That is the failure the cookbook calls reply-to-fallback-loops, and
# it was observed here before it was fixed.
#
# So: phase B is recognised POSITIVELY (hop.operation == "search", or "bundle"
# since GH #482 gave a catalogue lookup a second leg) -- and
# ONLY for a reply that carries no error_code. The store writes `operation`
# unconditionally and `error_code` on top of it (store/output.rs -- and since
# GH #331 the error paths stamp `operation` too, so `error_code` is the ONLY
# thing that tells a failure from an answer), so a
# FAILED search arrives looking exactly like a successful one; reading it as
# phase B rendered the error text as zero rows and handed the build an
# honest-looking empty briefing (GH #308).
#
# Anything else that arrives with a hop already set is TERMINAL -- the
# librarian degrades to a briefing that SAYS SO, and the build carries on
# without patterns. Retrieval is an enhancement; it must never be able to
# hang a build, and it must never pass a failure off as a zero-hit.
#
# The incoming message and this cell's OWN configuration arrive on the same
# stdin document: `params` is one of its three top-level objects, beside
# `envelope` and `body`, and the substrate always sets it ({} when there is
# nothing to hand over). Every knob below is read from it, so each one is
# per-INSTANCE configuration -- two librarians in one colony are tuned apart,
# and a mutation retunes one of them without touching a colony-wide
# environment (GH #138, ruling R-0904-6). The literal beside each name is the
# shipped default; it is the same number the template config and
# `contract.settings` carry, and a test pins the three against each other.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
hop = (envelope.get("header") or {}).get("hop") or {}
msgs = d.get("messages") or []
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    # A knob explicitly set to null or to whitespace is "not configured", not a
    # crash: an operator who blanks a line in a config means the default.
    v = P.get(key, default)
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)

# GH #482 -- the two legs of a catalogue lookup, addressed by NAME.
#
# The store answers a bundle with one `tool_result` turn per leg, keyed on that
# leg's `tool_call_id` (store/output.rs, `build_bundle_result`), and it keys the
# single turn of a one-op reply exactly the same way (`build_tool_result`). So a
# slot name is the address in both shapes. The positional read this cell used
# before survives only as the fallback for a reply that carries no id at all --
# and only where there is no second leg it could be confused with.
SEARCH_SLOT = "lib1"
NAMES_SLOT = "lib-names"


def slot_text(slot):
    for m in msgs:
        if m.get("id") == slot and m.get("text"):
            return m["text"]
    return ""


def first_text():
    for m in msgs:
        if m.get("text"):
            return m["text"]
    return ""


def has_slot(slot):
    """Whether a leg answered AT ALL. An empty appeal and an absent one are
    different facts -- the first says the catalogue holds no names, the second
    says nobody asked -- and only one of them may put a verdict in a briefing."""
    return any(m.get("id") == slot for m in msgs)


def rows_of(raw):
    """The slate one leg came back with. A store error text parses as neither a
    list nor JSON, and a non-list is not a slate."""
    try:
        v = json.loads(raw or "null")
    except Exception:
        return []
    return v if isinstance(v, list) else []


def leg_error(slot):
    """The `error_code` of ONE leg of a bundle. A bundle never reports a leg's
    failure in the header -- `bundle_errors` counts them and the header's own
    `error_code` keeps its hard meaning of "the whole reply is a refusal" -- so
    the per-leg code lives in the body's `results[]` slot."""
    for r in (d.get("results") or []):
        if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("tool_call_id") == slot and r.get("error_code"):
            return str(r["error_code"])
    return ""


# GH #511 -- the retriever's own truncation, and it is PER KIND and NAMED.
#
# It was `text[:1200]`: silent, mid-word, and the same number for every row.
# Measured over the shipped corpus, 330 of 603 rows were cut -- and 80 of the 87
# CATALOGUE rows, which is the class where the cut does the damage. A catalogue
# row is `CONTRACT --`, `STORES --`, `PARAMS --` and then the whole
# `template.json`, and `description.examples` is the LAST key of every one of
# them, so the cut landed every time on the only place a template's worked
# instantiation is published. One measured wish looked `clock` up three times,
# got the identical cut row back each time -- `schedules` 0, `emit_to` 0 -- read
# the corpus as exhausted, and spent its whole repair budget guessing the two
# param names the row already carried (GH #508).
#
# THREE windows, because the three lookups ask different questions:
#
# * A CATALOGUE row (kind == "template") travels WHOLE. `catalogue_lookup` is a
#   targeted question about ONE named template, and the row IS that template's
#   interface; half an interface is not a smaller answer, it is a wrong one. The
#   window is the corpus generator's own chunk cap
#   (workshop/tools/build_librarian_seed.py, MAX_CHARS), so a catalogue row is
#   bounded by the discipline that WROTE it (GH #344) instead of being cut a
#   second time here, and the worst case stays countable: TOPK rows of that size.
# * A LEVEL row (kind == "level") travels whole too, in its own window. It is
#   the COMPLETE transit edge set a composition level gives a new child, and a
#   set published half is a set that will be drawn half -- a level wired with
#   nine of its nineteen edges boots and answers nothing on the lanes nobody
#   drew. It had lived inside the 1200 with 14 characters to spare, which is not
#   a margin but a coincidence: GH #543 gave the assistant level the way back
#   from a screen and the row measured 1286. Trimming the header a fifth time
#   would buy the next edge and no more, so the promise
#   (`a_level_row_survives_the_retriever_whole`) is kept by a mechanism instead
#   of by thrift. Six rows exist at all, so the worst case is countable here too.
# * Every other row keeps the 1200-character window. `librarian_search` is a
#   RECALL question -- five rows out of six hundred -- where breadth is what is
#   being paid for and the round budget is what limits it (GH #485).
#
# And no cut is silent again. It lands on a word boundary and it SAYS what it
# did, the way the generator's `-cont` rows say "continued": a fragment a reader
# knows is a fragment is a different object from one it does not.
ROW_CHARS = _int("row_chars", 1200)
CATALOGUE_CHARS = _int("catalogue_chars", 4000)
LEVEL_CHARS = _int("level_chars", 1600)
TOPK = _int("topk", 5)

CAPS = {"template": lambda: CATALOGUE_CHARS, "level": lambda: LEVEL_CHARS}


def window(body, kind):
    """As much of `body` as this KIND of row may spend, plus a MARKER when that
    was not all of it. A window of 0 or less means no cut at all."""
    cap = CAPS[kind]() if kind in CAPS else ROW_CHARS
    if cap <= 0 or len(body) <= cap:
        return body
    head = body[:cap]
    # A line break is the best seam, a space the next best -- the same order the
    # corpus chunker uses. A seam in the first half of the window would throw
    # away more than the cut does, so an unbroken run that long is cut hard and
    # still marked.
    seam = max(head.rfind("\n"), head.rfind(" "))
    if seam > cap // 2:
        head = head[:seam]
    head = head.rstrip()
    return ("%s\n\u2026 [TRUNCATED: %d of %d characters were not sent. This row "
            "is a FRAGMENT and not a whole statement. A template's own catalogue "
            "row is never cut -- ask catalogue_lookup for it by name.]"
            % (head, len(body) - len(head), len(body)))


text = first_text()

# A failed SEARCH leg is the same fact a one-op reply reports in
# `hop.error_code`, so it is lifted there instead of being handled a second
# time: the terminal branch below stays the ONE place that decides what a
# failure does, and GH #308 is not re-litigated per reply shape. A failed NAMES
# leg is deliberately NOT lifted -- the appeal is an enhancement on top of an
# enhancement, and losing it may not cost the briefing a single row.
if not hop.get("error_code"):
    _search_failed = leg_error(SEARCH_SLOT)
    if _search_failed:
        hop = dict(hop)
        hop["error_code"] = _search_failed

if hop.get("operation") in ("search", "bundle") and not hop.get("error_code"):
    # ---- Phase B: rows back from the store, turn them into a briefing.
    #
    # The original request travels in the CONTEXT compartment (hop is per-hop
    # and the store overwrites it), put there by the edge modifier that reads
    # hop.orig on the way out. Without it phase B would hand the authoring cell
    # a pile of patterns and no question -- and, since GH #482, nothing to
    # check the catalogue's names against.
    ctx = (envelope.get("header") or {}).get("context") or {}
    original = ctx.get("orig_request") or ""

    raw = slot_text(SEARCH_SLOT)
    if not raw and not has_slot(NAMES_SLOT):
        raw = text
    rows = rows_of(raw)
    brief = []
    for r in rows[:TOPK]:
        # The row id belongs in the heading because source+section+kind stopped
        # being unique (GH #344): a section over 4000 characters is carried in
        # continuation rows that share all three, so two pieces of one section
        # would arrive under the SAME heading with different bodies and nothing
        # saying which is which -- or that either is a fragment. The id says
        # which piece, and "continued" says the text starts mid-argument, which
        # is the part a model must not read as a whole statement.
        doc_id = r.get("id") or "?"
        brief.append("### %s -- %s (%s) [%s]\n%s" % (
            r.get("source", "?"), r.get("section", "?"), r.get("kind", "?"),
            doc_id + (", continued" if "-cont" in doc_id else ""),
            window(r.get("text") or "", r.get("kind"))))

    # ---- GH #482: the catalogue's NAME APPEAL, and the verdict it buys.
    #
    # `catalogue_lookup` is BM25 and always hands back its best hits, so a
    # caller could not tell `not found` from `found something adjacent` and had
    # no reason to stop asking. Measured on one wish: seven rounds of the same
    # four questions rephrased, a prompt growing 5 557 -> 50 220 tokens, and no
    # manifest at the end of it. The appeal is the second leg of the same
    # bundle -- every `section` the catalogue holds, which for a catalogue row
    # IS the template name -- and the verdict goes in FRONT of the rows,
    # because a reader that meets four plausible neighbours first has already
    # begun reading them as the answer.
    names = sorted(n for n in {str(r.get("section") or "")
                               for r in rows_of(slot_text(NAMES_SLOT))} if n)
    named = []
    if names:
        # LONGEST first, and a match is struck out of the haystack, so
        # `builder-librarian` is never also reported as `builder`. Word
        # boundaries are what keep `member` out of `remember` and
        # `membership`; a hyphen is a non-word character, so a hyphenated name
        # carries boundaries of its own at both ends -- which is the only
        # reason the multi-word names in this catalogue (`daily-digest`,
        # `memory-hive`, `session-keeper`) can be matched at all.
        hay = " %s " % original.lower()
        for n in sorted(names, key=lambda s: (-len(s), s)):
            pat = re.compile(r"\b%s\b" % re.escape(n.lower()))
            if pat.search(hay):
                named.append(n)
                hay = pat.sub(lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), hay)
        named.sort()

    # The two answer forms, and they are the ones the template's `description`
    # and README publish verbatim.
    verdict = ""
    if names and named:
        verdict = ("the request names templates that exist: %s. The rows below "
                   "are the catalogue's answer for them." % ", ".join(named))
    elif names:
        verdict = ("no template by that name. The catalogue holds %d names: %s. "
                   "Anything below is a nearest neighbour by text and not a "
                   "name an `add_nodes` can use." % (len(names), ", ".join(names)))

    rendered = "\n\n".join(brief) if brief else "(no matching patterns)"
    if verdict:
        rendered = verdict + "\n\n" + rendered

    header = {"route": "brief", "stage": "briefed", "hits": len(rows)}
    if has_slot(NAMES_SLOT):
        # The verdict is MEASURED and not merely spoken: how many names the
        # catalogue answered with, and whether the request held one of them.
        # Stamped only where the appeal was actually made, so an unmarked
        # `librarian_search` emits the header it always did.
        header["catalogue_names"] = len(names)
        header["catalogue_named"] = 1 if named else 0

    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": header,
        "messages": [
            {"origin": "user", "type": "text", "text": original, "id": ""},
            {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "text": rendered, "id": ""},
        ],
    }))
    sys.exit(0)

if hop.get("error_code") or hop.get("stage") == "briefed":
    # ---- Terminal: retrieval failed. Say so, and stop.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"route": "brief", "stage": "briefed", "hits": 0, "degraded": True},
        "messages": [
            {"origin": "user", "type": "text",
             "text": ((envelope.get("header") or {}).get("context") or {}).get("orig_request") or "",
             "id": ""},
            {"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
             "text": "(retrieval unavailable: %s)" % (
                 hop.get("error_code") or "unexpected reply"),
             "id": ""}],
    }))
    sys.exit(0)

# ---- Phase A: request in, build a BM25 query.
#
# FTS5 treats punctuation as syntax, so a raw natural-language sentence is not a
# safe query string. Reduce to word tokens and OR them: recall matters more than
# precision here because the ranking, not the filter, is what surfaces the good
# chunk.
words = [w for w in re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,}", text.lower())]
stop = {"the", "and", "for", "that", "with", "this", "from", "into", "have",
        "you", "are", "was", "not", "but", "can", "will", "would", "should",
        "mir", "einen", "eine", "der", "die", "das", "und", "mit", "bau",
        "baue", "build", "make", "create", "please", "want", "need"}
#
# Each term travels as a QUOTED PHRASE. A bare hyphen is FTS5 syntax, so
# `daily-digest OR cell` came back `no such column: digest` -- and every
# multi-word template name in this corpus is hyphenated (`daily-digest`,
# `memory-hive`, `builder-librarian`, `session-keeper`), which made the query the
# librarian exists to serve the query that could not run (GH #308). The
# quoted spelling means "these tokens, adjacent", which is what a hyphenated
# name is. The double quote is stripped from every token first, so nothing
# in a request can break out of the quoting.
terms = [w.replace('"', "") for w in words if w not in stop][:12]
terms = [w for w in terms if w]
query = " OR ".join('"%s"' % w for w in terms) if terms else '"cell"'

op = {"operation": "search", "table": "docs", "match": query,
      "columns": ["id", "source", "section", "kind", "text"],
      "limit": TOPK}

# GH #483 -- the KIND filter, which was declared and never applied.
#
# `templates/builder/lib` stamps hop.lib_kind == "template" for a
# `catalogue_lookup` and its own description promises "the same corpus filtered
# to the rows that describe a template". Nothing read the key: both tools ran
# the identical unfiltered BM25 query, and a catalogue lookup for `member` came
# back with `org` at position one and `member` at position four, as a
# continuation chunk. A tool that answers a different question than the one its
# schema names is a tool a model cannot learn to use -- measured in the design
# runs of GH #485, where four of the fifteen retrieval rounds were the same
# lookup asked again.
#
# `search` filters the BASE table beside the MATCH (store/ops.rs, op_search), so
# this costs one key and no second query.
kind = str(hop.get("lib_kind") or "").strip()
if kind:
    op["where"] = {"kind": kind}

ops = [(SEARCH_SLOT, op)]
if kind == "template":
    # GH #482 -- the NAME APPEAL rides along, as a SECOND op in the SAME
    # message. The store runs a bundle's ops in order over its one connection
    # and answers with one `tool_result` turn per leg, so this costs one round
    # trip and no second lookup. A catalogue row's `section` IS the template
    # name (`access`, `daily-digest`, `builder-librarian`) and its `source` is
    # that template's `template.json`, so the name list is one column of the
    # rows already indexed -- no new table, no new seed.
    #
    # The limit is deliberately far above the corpus: the catalogue is 92 rows
    # for 43 names today, and a list that gets CUT would answer "these are the
    # names there are" with a subset, which is worse than not answering. 500
    # leaves the library room to grow several times over before the number has
    # to be looked at again.
    ops.append((NAMES_SLOT, {"operation": "select", "table": "docs",
                             "columns": ["section"], "where": {"kind": kind},
                             "limit": 500}))

sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": {"route": "lsearch", "librarian_query": query, "orig": text,
               "lib_kind": kind},
    "messages": [
        # A UBF turn object allows exactly origin/type/text/id
        # (schemas/ubf-body.json, TurnObject: additionalProperties false), so
        # the op travels in `text` and nowhere else.
        {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": slot,
         "text": json.dumps(o)}
        for slot, o in ops
    ],
}))

row_chars.description: Window of an ORDINARY rendered row, in characters. A row that did not fit is cut on a word boundary and says so. `librarian_search` is a recall question -- five rows out of six hundred -- so breadth is what this number buys and the round budget is what limits it.

catalogue_chars.description: Window of a CATALOGUE row (kind `template`), in characters. It is the corpus generator's own chunk cap (workshop/tools/build_librarian_seed.py, MAX_CHARS), so such a row travels whole: a catalogue row IS a template's interface, and half an interface is a wrong answer rather than a shorter one.

level_chars.description: Window of a LEVEL row (kind `level`), in characters. A level row is the COMPLETE transit edge set a composition level gives a new child, and a set published half is a set that will be drawn half.

topk.description: How many rows one lookup asks the store for and renders. It is the store `limit` and the render bound in one, so raising it costs prompt on every retrieval round.

description.purpose: The query/brief state machine of `builder-librarian`: phase A turns a request into a BM25 query the store's FTS5 index accepts, phase B renders the rows it gets back into a briefing for the authoring cell behind the librarian. No state, no writes, and a third terminal branch that says so when retrieval failed.
description.use_when: Reached on `in_request` from the librarian hive, and again on the store's reply over the hive's own return edge. Nothing else addresses it.
description.not_in_scope: It does not rank -- BM25 in the store does. It does not hold the corpus, and it never writes one: the seed is a build product of the repository's corpus generator. It does not decide what a degraded round means; it marks it and lets the model weigh it. Retrieval is an enhancement, so no branch here may end without a briefing.
description.emits_meaning: route lsearch is phase A -- the store op (or, for a catalogue lookup, the two store ops) as `tool_call` turns in one message; hop.librarian_query is the query as FTS5 will read it, hop.orig the request the return edge promotes into context, hop.lib_kind the corpus filter a `catalogue_lookup` asks for. route brief is phase B and the terminal branch -- hop.hits counts the rows, hop.degraded marks a briefing that stands in for a failed lookup, and hop.stage == 'briefed' is the marker the hive routes out on. A CATALOGUE LOOKUP (hop.lib_kind == 'template') answers in one further, documented form, and it is the whole point of asking the catalogue for its own names beside the search: the briefing OPENS with the verdict on the name. Where the request holds a name the catalogue has, the head line reads `the request names templates that exist: <names>. The rows below are the catalogue's answer for them.` Where it holds none, the head line reads `no template by that name. The catalogue holds <n> names: <every name, comma separated>. Anything below is a nearest neighbour by text and not a name an `add_nodes` can use.` -- so a caller can tell `not found` from `found something adjacent` in ONE round instead of rephrasing the same question until its budget is gone. hop.catalogue_names counts the names the catalogue answered with and hop.catalogue_named is 1 or 0, so the verdict is measured rather than asserted; both are absent from an unmarked `librarian_search`, which never asks. EVERY RENDERED ROW IS WINDOWED, and the window is per kind: a CATALOGUE row (kind 'template') travels WHOLE, because that row IS the template's interface and half an interface is a wrong answer rather than a shorter one; a LEVEL row (kind 'level') gets a window of its own at `params.level_chars`, because a complete edge set published half is a set that will be drawn half; every other row is windowed at `params.row_chars`. A row that did not fit is cut on a word boundary and SAYS SO, in the line `… [TRUNCATED: <n> of <m> characters were not sent. This row is a FRAGMENT and not a whole statement. A template's own catalogue row is never cut -- ask catalogue_lookup for it by name.]` -- the same discipline the corpus generator's `-cont` rows follow, because a fragment a reader knows is a fragment is a different object from one it does not (GH #344, GH #511).
description.consumes_meaning: body.messages carries the request (phase A: the first turn with text) or the store's slate (phase B: the `tool_result` turn keyed `lib1`, and the catalogue's name appeal keyed `lib-names`). body.results carries the per-leg metadata of a bundle, which is the only place a single failed leg reports its error_code -- a failed search leg degrades the briefing, a failed name appeal costs it nothing. context.orig_request is the question the briefing hands on and the string the name check runs against.
